summary: The video presents how modern purchasing decisions are heavily influenced by online conversations rather than marketer-led content. It notes that customers spend only about 20% of their decision-making time listening to brands and reading marketing material, while roughly 80% comes from input from colleagues, friends, and strangers on the internet. The content references Yelp and other websites as sources of public opinion, framing this online chatter as a form of social proof. It introduces the Keller K. Chalk Track as a way to track sentiment and the extent to which people embrace and use social media in their buying decisions.
title: Online Reviews, Social Proof, and the Keller K Chalk Track
